questions.q: In FeedbackScope's Dockerfile, what stays confined to the builder stage and never reaches the final image?
options: Build tools and compilers used while installing Python packages
The application's app.py file
The uvicorn server that runs the app
The exposed port number
questions.explain: Only the installed packages get copied into the final stage -- the build tooling used to install them stays behind in the builder stage.

questions.q: Why does the Dockerfile run a line that loads the sentiment-analysis pipeline during the build itself?
options: To validate the Python syntax only
To reduce the number of Dockerfile stages
To download and cache the model weights at build time, avoiding a first-request download delay
To test the health check endpoint before deployment
questions.explain: Running the pipeline during build forces the model weights to download into the image itself, so a running container never pays that cost on its first real request.

questions.q: Why does this lesson tag the image 'v1' instead of just 'latest'?
options: Because 'latest' is not a valid Docker tag
Because a specific version tag is what gives a rollback something concrete to roll back to
Because v1 builds faster than latest
Because container registries reject the 'latest' tag
questions.explain: Lesson 16's rollback strategy needs a specific previous tag to target -- 'latest' alone doesn't give you that.

questions.q: What does deploying FeedbackScope in this lesson reuse from Lesson 12?
options: A requirement to use AWS App Runner specifically, with no alternative
The same rollback mechanism used for rolling updates
The exact same container image, unmodified
The two-screen pattern: point the platform at the image and port, then add a health check
questions.explain: This capstone deploy step is explicitly the same build-config / service-config pattern taught in Lesson 12.

questions.q: What does this lesson say is deliberately still missing after this deploy, to be added in Lesson 24?
options: A real autoscaling policy beyond the platform's defaults, plus caching
The Dockerfile itself
The container registry push
The application's source code
questions.explain: This lesson's job was only getting a working, publicly reachable container running -- autoscaling and caching are explicitly left for Lesson 24.
